title: Impact of Mass Deworming on School Attendance

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Two-period Difference-in-Differences (DID), implemented as a two-way fixed effects (TWFE) regression: y_it = α_i + λ_t + β (Treated_i × Post_t) + ε_it.
- Why: We have treated and control schools observed before and after the deworming rollout. The interaction term identifies the causal effect under standard DID assumptions.
- Key assumptions:
  - Parallel trends: In the absence of the program, treated and control schools would have experienced the same change in attendance over time.
  - No spillovers/interference: The program at treated schools does not affect attendance at control schools (important given potential epidemiological externalities).
  - Stable composition and measurement: No selective changes in who is measured and consistent measurement of attendance over time.
  - No other contemporaneous shocks differentially affecting treated vs. control schools.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code

# 0) Setup ----------------------------------------------------------------------
required_pkgs <- c("readr", "dplyr", "fixest", "sandwich", "lmtest")
to_install <- setdiff(required_pkgs, rownames(installed.packages()))
if(length(to_install) > 0) install.packages(to_install, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")

library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(fixest)
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)

# 1) Read data ------------------------------------------------------------------
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s49_data.csv"
df <- read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE)

# Basic checks
cat("N obs:", nrow(df), "\n")
cat("Unique units:", length(unique(df$unit_id)), "\n")
cat("Unique periods:", length(unique(df$period)), "\n")
cat("Share treated:", mean(df$treated), "\n")
cat("Share post:", mean(df$post), "\n\n")

# Ensure variables are in expected format
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    unit_id = as.integer(unit_id),
    treated = as.integer(treated),
    post    = as.integer(post)
  )

# 2) Core DID (TWFE with unit and time FE, clustered SE by unit) ----------------
# y_it = alpha_i + lambda_t + beta*(treated_i * post_t) + e_it
m_twfe <- feols(y ~ treated:post | unit_id + period, data = df, cluster = ~ unit_id)

# Extract results
coefs_twfe <- broom::tidy(m_twfe, conf.int = TRUE)
beta_row <- coefs_twfe[coefs_twfe$term == "treated:post", ]

# 3) Simple DID OLS with cluster-robust SE --------------------------------------
m_ols <- lm(y ~ treated + post + treated:post, data = df)
vc_ols <- sandwich::vcovCL(m_ols, cluster = ~ unit_id)
ols_ct <- lmtest::coeftest(m_ols, vcov. = vc_ols)
beta_ols <- ols_ct["treated:post", 1]
se_ols   <- ols_ct["treated:post", 2]
t_ols    <- ols_ct["treated:post", 3]
p_ols    <- ols_ct["treated:post", 4]
ci_ols   <- beta_ols + c(-1, 1) * qnorm(0.975) * se_ols

# 4) Manual 2x2 DID (difference in means) ---------------------------------------
mean_t_post <- df %>% filter(treated == 1, post == 1) %>% summarize(m = mean(y)) %>% pull(m)
mean_t_pre  <- df %>% filter(treated == 1, post == 0) %>% summarize(m = mean(y)) %>% pull(m)
mean_c_post <- df %>% filter(treated == 0, post == 1) %>% summarize(m = mean(y)) %>% pull(m)
mean_c_pre  <- df %>% filter(treated == 0, post == 0) %>% summarize(m = mean(y)) %>% pull(m)
did_manual  <- (mean_t_post - mean_t_pre) - (mean_c_post - mean_c_pre)

# 5) First-difference (ANCOVA-style) robustness ---------------------------------
# Collapse to unit-level change: dy_i = y_post - y_pre; regress dy on treated
dy_df <- df %>%
  group_by(unit_id) %>%
  summarize(
    treated = first(treated),
    dy = mean(y[post == 1]) - mean(y[post == 0]),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

m_diff <- lm(dy ~ treated, data = dy_df)
vc_diff <- sandwich::vcovHC(m_diff, type = "HC1")
diff_ct <- lmtest::coeftest(m_diff, vcov. = vc_diff)
beta_diff <- diff_ct["treated", 1]
se_diff   <- diff_ct["treated", 2]
p_diff    <- diff_ct["treated", 4]
ci_diff   <- beta_diff + c(-1, 1) * qnorm(0.975) * se_diff

# 6) Trimmed-sample robustness (drop 2.5% tails of y) ---------------------------
q_lo <- quantile(df$y, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE)
q_hi <- quantile(df$y, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE)
df_trim <- df %>% filter(y >= q_lo, y <= q_hi)

m_twfe_trim <- feols(y ~ treated:post | unit_id + period, data = df_trim, cluster = ~ unit_id)
coefs_trim <- broom::tidy(m_twfe_trim, conf.int = TRUE)
beta_row_trim <- coefs_trim[coefs_trim$term == "treated:post", ]

# 7) Print clear numerical results ----------------------------------------------
cat("Main DID estimate (TWFE, clustered by unit):\n")
cat(sprintf("  beta = %.4f,  SE = %.4f,  95%% CI [%.4f, %.4f],  p = %.4f\n",
            beta_row$estimate, beta_row$std.error, beta_row$conf.low, beta_row$conf.high, beta_row$p.value))

cat("\nRobustness checks:\n")
cat(sprintf("- OLS DID (treated + post + interaction), clustered by unit:\n  beta = %.4f, SE = %.4f, 95%% CI [%.4f, %.4f], p = %.4f\n",
            beta_ols, se_ols, ci_ols[1], ci_ols[2], p_ols))
cat(sprintf("- Manual 2x2 DID (difference in means):\n  DID = %.4f\n", did_manual))
cat(sprintf("- First-difference at unit level (dy ~ treated):\n  beta = %.4f, SE = %.4f, 95%% CI [%.4f, %.4f], p = %.4f\n",
            beta_diff, se_diff, ci_diff[1], ci_diff[2], p_diff))
cat(sprintf("- TWFE on trimmed sample (2.5%% tails removed), clustered by unit:\n  beta = %.4f, SE = %.4f, 95%% CI [%.4f, %.4f], p = %.4f\n",
            beta_row_trim$estimate, beta_row_trim$std.error, beta_row_trim$conf.low, beta_row_trim$conf.high, beta_row_trim$p.value))

# 8) Pre-period balance check on y ----------------------------------------------
pre_balance <- df %>%
  filter(post == 0) %>%
  summarize(
    mean_t = mean(y[treated == 1]),
    mean_c = mean(y[treated == 0]),
    diff   = mean(y[treated == 1]) - mean(y[treated == 0])
  )
cat("\nPre-period balance (mean attendance y, pre only):\n")
print(pre_balance)
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: We expect a non-negative effect (zero to modest positive) of deworming on attendance. A negative β (treated × post) would indicate unintended adverse effects; theory and prior evidence suggest this is unlikely.
- Magnitude: If y is measured in standard deviations (as the preview suggests), a plausible effect is between 0 and +0.10 SD. If y were in percentage points of attendance, we would expect 0 to +2 pp. Any materially negative and statistically significant effect would be surprising and warrant investigation of mechanisms (e.g., short-run illness from treatment, timing conflicts, or reporting changes).

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in attendance rates over time between treated and untreated schools.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The mass deworming program is associated with a decrease in school attendance rates.
